Refactor the `Trie` implementation to improve its overall structure and maintainability.
Abstract the character mapping logic into a dedicated helper method to decouple the Trie implementation from the specific encoding scheme (e.g., lowercase 'a'-'z').
Introduce a `TrieNode` factory method or constructor that encapsulates the initialization of the `children` array to further clean up the `TrieNode` definition.
Extract the Trie data structure into its own separate file to adhere to the principle of single responsibility and improve file organization.

Replace the hardcoded `ALPHABET_START` and `ALPHABET_SIZE` constants with an injectable character mapping strategy or configuration object to allow the `Trie` to support different character sets without modifying its internal code.

Encapsulate the `TrieNode` children array management within the `TrieNode` class by introducing methods like `getChild(char)`, `setChild(char, TrieNode)`, and `hasChild(char)` to remove direct array access from the `Trie` class.
Introduce a `Trie` operation `delete(String key)` using a recursive approach to remove nodes that no longer contribute to any stored words, ensuring the memory footprint is minimized after removals.

Refactor the `Trie` class by introducing a `TrieIterator` or an implementation of `Iterable<String>` to support lexicographical traversal of all stored words, allowing users to easily retrieve or list the contents of the trie.

Extract the `TrieIterator` into a standalone, top-level static class within the same package, or ensure it is appropriately decoupled from the internal `Trie` implementation details to improve testability and promote cleaner separation between the container and its iteration logic.

Implement a `size()` method in `Trie` and consider caching the word count, ensuring it is correctly updated during `insert()` and `delete()` operations to provide O(1) retrieval of the number of words stored in the trie.
